newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil's Cardoso wants quick civil service reform.
newsitem.headline: Brazil's Cardoso wants quick civil service reform.

text.p: Brazilian President Fernando Henrique Cardoso, seeking to take advantage of Tuesday's vote in favor of his re-election plan, said he wanted Congress to quickly restart work on a reform of the civil service.
"I have asked Congress to vote on the administrative reform, if possible during the extraordinary session," Cardoso told a gathering of deputies.
A month-long extraordinary session of Congress, called principally to get a re-election constitutional amendment through the lower house, is due to finish on February 6.

The civil service reform aims to help state and municipal governments get their finances in order, principally by allowing them to dismiss workers, who currently cannot be fired, and spend money on investment rather than payrolls.

The reform has been approved in its lower house committee but its first of two votes on the floor of the Chamber of Deputies was put on hold as the government focused its efforts on approving the re-election amendment.

A government source in Congress said he thought any resuscitation of the civil service reform would have to wait until after the re-election bill is put to its second and final vote in the lower house, expected around February 15.

"The new mayors are pressing the government very hard for approval of the reform because it will help them govern but the second round of voting on re-election will have to come first," said the source, who asked not to be identified.
